title.narrative: Trade and Supply Chain Finance Program

description.narrative: Australia's investment in the Asian Development Bank's Trade and Supply Chain Finance Program supports banks and micro, small and medium sized enterprises in developing countries and least developed countries in the Indo-Pacific to strengthen trade finance capacity and accessibility. Australia's contribution includes a focus on Asia-Pacific Economic Cooperation (APEC) and Indo-Pacific Economic Framework (IPEF) economies. The Program aims to help close the global trade finance gap by addressing information asymmetries and changing perceptions of risks in the region.

participating-org.narrative: AUSTRALIA - Department of Foreign Affairs and Trade

organisation.narrative: Australia - Department of Foreign Affairs and Trade

description.narrative: Australia’s support for the Asian Development Bank's Trade and Supply Chain Finance Program (ADB TSCFP) enabled participation of 270 women entrepreneurs in a forum to help address challenges faced by women exporters, from trade finance to the lack of information and knowledge of trade-related policies. Organised in conjunction with the Indonesia-Australia Comprehensive Economic Partnership (IA-CEPA) economic cooperation program, Katalis, the forum helped build participant capacity, including through peer-to-peer learning and knowledge sharing, on cross border trade.

Through our investment with the Asian Development Bank's Trade and Supply Chain Finance Program (ADB TSCFP), Australia supported capacity building on trade finance for Pacific banks and businesses through a forum on strategies, challenges, and opportunities to facilitate trade and trade finance across the Pacific. Banks, regional region and international trade experts and businesses from across the region considered possible solutions to the challenges faced in the Pacific and heard about Australia’s commitment to work with Pacific island countries and public, private, and multilateral sector partners to address the decline of correspondent banking relationships (CBRs) in the Pacific. The forum was attended by 50 participants, including 18 women, fostering a diverse and inclusive discussion.
